Interactions is a conversational AI company that builds intelligent virtual assistants combining speech recognition, natural language understanding and human-assisted review, used to automate customer care calls and chats. Customers are large enterprises in telecom, financial services, healthcare and retail, who pay for software and usage-based services. Headquartered in Franklin, Massachusetts, it raised roughly $163 million in venture funding. It is a private B2B technology firm, so brand awareness among consumers is low and it is little known outside enterprise customer-service circles.

Italcer Group is an Italian ceramics manufacturer based in Rubiera in the Emilia-Romagna tile district near Modena. It produces indoor and outdoor porcelain stoneware tiles and slabs for floors, walls and facades, sold to builders, distributors, architects and retailers in Italy and export markets. The group was formed by combining several established ceramic brands under one holding and has received private-equity backed funding of about 150 million. It is a private B2B building-materials supplier with limited consumer brand awareness, though known within the architecture and design trade.

Kaltura is a video technology company offering cloud video platforms, lecture capture, webcasting, virtual events and video-in-the-cloud tools. Customers are universities, large enterprises, media companies and governments, who pay SaaS subscriptions and usage fees; its tools power online learning and corporate communications. Founded in 2006 with roots in Israel, it is headquartered in New York and listed on Nasdaq (KLTR) since its 2021 IPO. It is a B2B vendor with strong visibility among education and enterprise IT buyers but little consumer brand awareness.

Lashou.com was an early Chinese group-buying website, launched in 2010 and modelled on Groupon, offering daily discounted deals on restaurants, entertainment, beauty and travel in major cities. It earned commission from merchants selling vouchers. Based in Beijing, it raised about $165 million before the Chinese group-buying market consolidated in 2011-2012, when it lost ground to rivals such as Meituan and Dianping. It later filed for a US IPO but did not complete it, and it faded as a business. Consumer visibility was once high in China but is now minimal.

OneSource Virtual is a Dallas-based professional services firm that implements and supports Workday cloud software for human resources and finance, and also runs managed services and business process outsourcing for Workday customers. Clients are mid-size and large enterprises across industries, paying project and recurring service fees. It was among the larger Workday-focused partners and raised about $165 million of growth capital in 2015. Its current ownership should be checked. It is a B2B consultancy with little consumer brand visibility.

Paragon Print and Packaging Group is a United Kingdom manufacturer of printed food packaging and labels, based in Spalding, Lincolnshire, a centre of British fresh produce. It supplies packaging for the food and beverage sector, serving food producers and retailers with cartons, trays, sleeves and printed materials. It is a privately held B2B manufacturer that attracted about $167 million of investment in 2013 as part of a consolidation of packaging businesses. Consumers see its products on supermarket shelves but the company itself has almost no brand awareness, making it an unlikely sponsor.

PayEgis is a Beijing-based financial technology provider offering digital infrastructure for the financial industry, including blockchain, cloud-native and security technology for banks, payment institutions and other regulated firms. It sells platforms and technology services to financial institutions and enterprises rather than to consumers. It raised about CN 1.07 billion in funding, a round dated July 2019, and is regarded as a Chinese fintech with ties to the Ant Group ecosystem. It is a B2B software provider with little public brand awareness outside the Chinese financial technology sector.

Powa Technologies was a London-based mobile commerce company that offered mobile shopping and payment technology, including its PowaTag product, which let consumers buy items by scanning images in print, TV or online. It sold software to retailers and brands and also ran Powa-branded retail technology. It raised roughly $177 million, was valued at around $2 billion at its peak in 2015, and collapsed into administration in 2016 after financial difficulties and a governance scandal. It is now defunct, so it is not a viable sponsorship prospect.

Rentvine is a cloud-based property management software company based in Estero, Florida. Its platform handles rent collection, accounting, maintenance, owner portals and tenant communication for residential property managers, who pay monthly subscription fees. The Crunchbase listing shows it raised about $174 million, with a round dated November 2024, which is a large figure for a firm of this kind. It serves small and mid-size property management companies in the United States and is a B2B software vendor with low consumer brand awareness.

Sentient Technologies was a San Francisco artificial intelligence company working on distributed machine learning, evolutionary algorithms and deep learning, with products for e-commerce personalisation (Sentient Aware) and financial trading. Customers were retailers and financial firms. It raised about $174 million and was one of the most heavily funded AI startups, but it wound down in 2018 and its assets were sold; the evolutionary AI business continued as Cognizant Evolutionary AI. The brand is effectively defunct, with minimal public visibility and no sponsorship potential.

Silver Peak Systems was a Santa Clara software-defined wide area network (SD-WAN) and WAN optimisation vendor, selling Unity EdgeConnect appliances and software to enterprises, telecoms and governments to connect branch offices and cloud services. It raised about $176 million in venture funding and was acquired by Aruba, a Hewlett Packard Enterprise company, in 2020 for roughly $925 million. It has been absorbed into HPE Aruba's networking portfolio. It was a B2B brand known to network engineers, with no consumer awareness.

THQ Nordic is a video game publisher and developer headquartered in Vienna, Austria, part of the listed Swedish Embracer Group. It owns franchises such as Darksiders, Titan Quest, Gothic, Destroy All Humans and the SpongeBob games, and publishes both new titles and remakes. Customers are gamers on PC and consoles, with revenue from game sales. Formerly Nordic Games, it was renamed in 2016 and was a reasonably well-known brand among gamers, though not a mainstream consumer name.

Ujjivan Financial Services is an Indian microfinance and later banking group headquartered in Bangalore. It started in 2005 serving low-income customers with small loans, mostly to women in groups, and its subsidiary became Ujjivan Small Finance Bank in 2017. The holding company is listed on Indian exchanges (NSE and BSE) and has millions of customers across many states. Customers are underserved households and small businesses. Brand awareness is solid in Indian retail banking but mostly among low-income and rural users.

Viveve Medical is a Colorado-based medical device company that developed the Geneveve system, a non-surgical radiofrequency treatment for vaginal laxity and sexual function in women after childbirth. It sold devices and single-use treatment tips to gynaecologists and aesthetic clinics in the United States and internationally. It raised roughly $173 million, was listed on Nasdaq (VIVE), and ran into financial trouble, filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023. It had limited consumer brand awareness and is no longer an active prospect.

Vlocity was a San Francisco software company that built industry-specific cloud applications on the Salesforce platform, covering communications, media, energy, insurance, health and public sector customers. It sold subscriptions to large enterprises needing customer, order and billing management. It raised about $163 million and was acquired by Salesforce in 2020 for about $1.33 billion, then rebranded as Salesforce Industries. The Vlocity brand has been retired inside Salesforce, so it is B2B with no standalone brand presence and no sponsorship rationale of its own.

Weidai is a Chinese online lending platform based in Hangzhou that connected individual lenders with borrowers, mainly through peer-to-peer car-collateral loans and consumer credit. It operated the Weidai app and earned fees from loan matching and services. It raised about CN 1.15 billion and listed on the NYSE as Weidai Ltd (WEI) in 2017, then declined sharply after Chinese regulators clamped down on peer-to-peer lending in 2018 to 2019. The brand has little international visibility.

Workday Adaptive Planning, formerly Adaptive Insights, is a cloud financial planning and analytics software provider, based in Palo Alto and Pleasanton, California. It sells budgeting, forecasting and reporting tools to finance teams of mid-size and large businesses on a subscription basis. It raised about $176 million before being acquired by Workday in 2018 for around $1.55 billion and rebranded as Workday Adaptive Planning. It is part of listed Workday (Nasdaq: WDAY). It is a B2B product with little consumer awareness.

1st Stop Group is a Blackpool-based United Kingdom financial services business that offers consumer and small business products, including loans, finance and insurance-related services, aimed at retail customers. It raised around 120 million in debt and equity funding in 2017. It is a privately held lender operating in the UK, with limited public detail available. Customers are mainly consumers seeking credit. It is a regional, low-profile finance brand, so awareness among the wider public is modest.

58fangdai is a China-based financial services and lending company in Nanjing, Jiangsu, with the Crunchbase description suggesting a national rental staging and living platform. The input shows it raised about $156 million, last dated January 2018, and is categorised under financial services and lending. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Affirmed Networks is a Massachusetts company that developed virtualised mobile core network software, notably its virtual evolved packet core, for mobile operators moving to 4G, 5G and cloud networks. Customers were carriers such as Vodafone, Orange and Telefonica. It raised about $155 million and was acquired by Microsoft in 2020 for a reported $1.35 billion, joining Azure for Operators. It was a B2B telecom software firm with no consumer brand awareness; the Affirmed name is no longer used independently.

Australian Foundation Investment Company (AFIC) is one of Australia's oldest and largest listed investment companies, managed from Melbourne and listed on the ASX (AFI). It holds a diversified portfolio of Australian shares for long-term capital growth and dividends, with a low-cost model and tens of thousands of retail shareholders. Founded in 1928, it manages billions of dollars of assets. It is a financial vehicle rather than a consumer brand, with awareness mainly among Australian investors and financial advisers.

Bitglass is a Campbell, California cybersecurity company that provided cloud access security broker (CASB) and secure access service edge (SASE) technology, protecting data across cloud apps, mobile devices and web traffic for enterprises. It raised about $150 million and was acquired by Forcepoint in 2024. Customers are large organisations in finance, healthcare and government. It sold subscriptions through channel partners and was a B2B brand known mainly to security teams, with no consumer visibility.

Data.ai, formerly App Annie, is a San Francisco mobile app and digital market data and analytics company. Its platform tracks downloads, revenue, usage and advertising for apps and games, selling subscriptions to publishers, brands, investors and consultants. Founded in 2010, it raised about $157 million and rebranded to Data.ai in 2022. It was acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024. The brand was well known in the mobile industry but is a B2B tool, not a consumer name.

Dixa is a Danish customer service software company headquartered in Copenhagen. Its cloud platform unifies calls, chat, email and messaging and uses AI to route and automate conversations for customer service teams. Customers are mid-size and large consumer-facing companies in Europe and North America, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2015 from a merger of Dixa and Elmer, it raised about $158 million, including a 2021 round. It is a B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness but strong presence at Nordic tech events.

Gainsight is a San Francisco customer success software company that created and leads the customer success category. Its platform helps subscription businesses track customer health, reduce churn and expand accounts, with products for customer success, product experience and customer communities. Customers are B2B software and services companies. It raised about $156 million and was acquired by private-equity firm Vista Equity Partners in 2020 for around $1.1 billion. It is a B2B brand with high recognition among SaaS professionals but none among consumers.

Golden Technology is a big data service company based in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, categorised under big data, blockchain and cloud services. The Crunchbase input shows it raised about $152 million, last dated October 2019, but gives little more about its products or customers. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Growth Opportunity Partners is a Cleveland, Ohio firm described as helping small businesses reach their growth goals through consulting and financial services, including capital for owner-led companies. The listing shows about $157 million raised, with the latest activity dated April 2024. It appears to be a private lender or investor serving small and mid-size United States businesses. It is a niche financial and advisory brand with little public awareness, and its customers are business owners rather than consumers.

GVK is an Indian conglomerate based in Hyderabad with interests in energy, airports, transportation, hospitality, resources and life sciences. It built power plants, operated Mumbai International Airport (through GVK Airport Holdings, later transferred to Adani Group in 2020-21) and ran the GVK Biosciences contract research arm. Customers range from state utilities and airlines to pharma companies. The group was founded in 1958 by G.V.K. Reddy and has had major debt problems. It is a recognised name in Indian business, but it is not a consumer brand.

HashCash Consultants is a software and blockchain technology company with a Palo Alto address, offering crypto exchange technology, wallet and custody services, payments and consulting. It sells white-label exchange software and development services to financial firms and crypto businesses, with operations in India and other markets. The listing shows about $150 million raised with the latest activity dated September 2017, which seems large for a firm of this kind. It is a B2B technology brand with limited public awareness.

IBK Capital is described as the venture capital arm of the Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK), based in Seoul, South Korea. The input shows about $150 million of funding with the latest date June 2026, and gives no further detail on its portfolio or size. It would invest in Korean startups and growth companies on behalf of its parent bank. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Jumei (Jumei International Holding) is a Chinese online beauty retailer founded in 2010 and based in Beijing. It sold cosmetics and skincare through flash sales and its Jumei.com platform, later expanding into other categories and its own content and brand business. It listed on the NYSE (JMEI) in 2014 and raised about $160 million. It was later taken private by its founder-led group. It was a well-known consumer shopping name in China but is little known abroad.

LeCloud is a Chinese cloud video and live streaming technology company based in Beijing, and part of LeEco (Letv) ecosystem. It provides video hosting, live streaming, content delivery and cloud services to media, sports and enterprise customers, and distributed content for LeSports and Letv. It raised about CN 1 billion in 2016. LeEco suffered a severe cash crisis from 2016 and was restructured, which weakened LeCloud's business. It is a B2B platform with limited awareness outside China.

Meetyou (Meet You) is a Xiamen-based Chinese women's health and lifestyle app group. Its Meiyou app helps users track periods, pregnancy and parenting, with community content, e-commerce and advertising as revenue sources. It reached over 100 million users in China, and raised around $158 million with a round dated August 2016. Meiyou filed for a Hong Kong IPO in 2018 and later more than once but had not listed at last report. It is a mass-market consumer app in China, mainly known among young female users.

Momondo Group is a Copenhagen-based travel search company behind the Momondo and Cheapflights metasearch sites, which compare flight, hotel and car-rental prices from many providers. It earns money from referral and advertising fees. Founded in 2006, it raised about $152 million, including a growth investment from General Atlantic and Cheapflights, and was acquired by Priceline Group (now Booking Holdings) in 2017 for about 550 million dollars. It runs consumer brands used in dozens of countries, with notable European brand recognition, and has used sports and entertainment marketing.

Practice Fusion was a San Francisco cloud-based electronic health record (EHR) company offering free, advertising-supported software to small doctor practices in the United States. It also sold data and services to pharma. It raised about $158 million and was acquired by Allscripts (now Veradigm) in 2018 for about $100 million. The company also settled a US Justice Department case in 2020 over opioid-related prompts in its software. It was a B2B healthcare IT brand with no consumer sponsorship profile and now operates inside Veradigm.

RadRock Tech is a Shenzhen, Guangdong-based company described as an innovative RFIC (radio frequency integrated circuit) design firm and categorised under industrial manufacturing. The input shows it raised about CN 1.08 billion, with the latest date December 2024. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Roobo is a Beijing hardware and artificial intelligence company that develops smart home and voice-interaction products, including smart speakers, AI robots for children and voice modules for other manufacturers. It sells devices and AI technology to consumer brands and OEMs, and it was reported to have supplied the smart speaker hardware behind some Chinese and international partner products. Founded in 2014, it raised about $153 million, with the latest round in 2017. It is mostly B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness outside China.

Sonatype is a Maryland software supply chain security company known for the Nexus repository manager and Maven Central, the main repository of Java open-source libraries. Its products scan open-source components for vulnerabilities and licence risk, and customers include large enterprises and government agencies. Founded in 2008 by Maven creator Jason van Zyl, it raised about $156 million and was acquired by Vista Equity Partners in 2019. Its brand is a B2B name well known among developers and DevSecOps teams, but unknown to the general public.

Spin Memory, formerly Spin Transfer Technologies, is a Fremont, California semiconductor company that develops magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) technology, including its orthogonal spin-transfer MRAM, for next-generation data storage and embedded memory. It licences intellectual property and works with chip foundries and manufacturers. It raised about $158 million. It is a deep-technology B2B firm with almost no consumer brand awareness, and its customers are chipmakers rather than end users.

TFI (Turkey) is described as a franchise of various restaurants, headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey. This is likely TFI TAB Gida, the Turkish franchisee behind Burger King, Popeyes and Sbarro in Turkey, but the input alone does not confirm this. The listing shows about $150 million of funding, last dated August 2016, under food and beverage and franchising. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

VDURA, formerly Panasas, is a Milpitas, California company that builds high-performance data storage and a data platform for AI and high-performance computing, selling storage systems and software to research labs, universities, media and energy companies, and enterprises. Panasas was founded in 1999 and rebranded to VDURA in 2024. It raised about $155 million in total. It is a specialised B2B technology brand known mostly among supercomputing and technical IT users, with essentially no consumer visibility.

Transcat is a Rochester, New York company that provides accredited calibration, repair, inspection and laboratory instrument services, and distributes test and measurement equipment. Customers are life sciences, aerospace and defence, industrial and energy firms across North America. It is listed on Nasdaq (TRNS), has operated for decades, and reports annual revenue of a few hundred million dollars. The listing shows about $150 million raised, last dated July 2025. It is a B2B business with little consumer awareness and low sponsorship potential.

2020 Bulkers was a Bermuda-incorporated dry bulk shipping company managing a fleet of modern, fuel-efficient Capesize vessels, listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange (2020). It earned money chartering ships to miners and commodity traders carrying iron ore, coal and bauxite. Its fleet details and current ownership should be checked. It was a B2B shipping company with essentially no consumer brand awareness and low sponsorship relevance, since it deals only with commodity charterers.

Mobile Infrastructure Corporation is a Cincinnati, Ohio real estate company that owns parking facilities, including garages and surface lots in major United States cities, and earns revenue from parking fees and leases to operators. Listed on the NYSE American (BEEP), it completed a merger with a SPAC in 2021. Its portfolio is dozens of parking assets across many United States metropolitan areas. It is a landlord rather than a consumer brand, with minimal public awareness.

Restoration Robotics was a medical device company that developed the ARTAS robotic system for hair transplantation, using image-guided robotics to harvest follicular units. Customers were physicians and clinics, with revenue from system sales and procedure-related supplies. It was listed on Nasdaq (HAIR) after a 2017 IPO, then merged with Venus Concept in 2019 and continues under the Venus Concept name. Venus Concept is based in Toronto, and the Restoration Robotics brand is no longer independent. It had limited consumer brand awareness.

Showroomprive is a French online flash-sales retailer of fashion, beauty, home and travel brands, founded in 2006 and based in La Plaine-Saint-Denis near Paris. It sells discounted branded goods in time-limited sales to millions of registered members, mainly in France and Europe. It was listed on Euronext Paris in 2015 and delisted after a takeover by its founders and Bpifrance-related backers in 2018-19. It is a well-known consumer e-commerce brand in France, with TV advertising and some sports sponsorship experience.

Zebit was a San Diego-based online retailer that offered interest-free instalment purchasing of consumer goods such as electronics, jewellery and home items to shoppers with limited credit, using its own payment-plan model. Revenue came from product margin and fees. It was reported to have raised about $145 million in debt and equity. It was small compared with mainstream retailers. Consumer awareness in the United States was modest, so it is no longer a likely sponsor prospect.

Tciplay Interactive Entertainment is a Shanghai, China company categorised under gaming, mobile and online games. The input shows funding of about CN 30 million, last dated July 2016, and lists it as a listed-company search result. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Agora is a real-time engagement platform provider that offers video, voice, live streaming and messaging APIs that developers embed in apps; customers include social, gaming, education and telehealth apps. It was founded in Shanghai in 2013 by Tony Zhao, with a major presence in Santa Clara, California. It listed on Nasdaq (API) in 2020, with Chinese and international customers. It is a B2B developer tool with little consumer visibility, although its technology powers well-known apps.

AInnovation is a Chinese artificial intelligence company based in Beijing (Haidian district) that provides AI-driven products and solutions for retail, manufacturing, finance and other industries, including computer vision and industrial optimisation. It sells software and projects to large enterprises and governments. It raised about CN 900 million, and filed for a Hong Kong IPO. It is a B2B technology firm with little brand awareness outside China's enterprise market.

Amaero International is a metal additive manufacturing company that produces advanced metal powders, such as titanium and refractory-alloy powders, for 3D printing in aerospace, defence and space. It is based in Tennessee after moving its main operations from Australia, and is listed on the ASX (3DA). Customers are manufacturers of aerospace and defence components. It is a specialised B2B supplier with low consumer awareness and a small share of the wider materials market.

Augmentum Fintech is a London-listed investment trust, quoted on the London Stock Exchange (AUGM), that invests in growth-stage financial technology companies, mainly in the UK and Europe. Its portfolio has included Zopa, Interactive Investor, Wefox and Chip. It is a financial investment vehicle rather than a consumer brand, with awareness limited to investors and fintech industry insiders, so it has little direct use for consumer sponsorship.

Avalon Advanced Materials is a Toronto-based Canadian exploration and development company focused on minerals for the clean-energy transition, notably the Separation Rapids lithium project in Ontario. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (AVL). It is pre-revenue and funds itself through equity raises and partnerships. It is a small resource company with essentially no consumer brand awareness and little capacity for large sponsorship deals.

Companhia Brasileira de Aluminio (Brazilian Aluminum Company, CBA) is a Sao Paulo-based aluminium producer that mines bauxite, refines alumina and smelts and rolls aluminium, selling to packaging, construction, automotive and energy customers; it also generates power. Part of the Votorantim group, it listed on the B3 exchange (CBAV3). It operates mainly in Brazil. It is a B2B industrial company, though products reach consumers in packaging and building products, with little brand awareness.

Chicago Atlantic BDC (formerly Silver Spike Investment Corp) is a Chicago-based business development company that lends to cannabis companies and other specialty borrowers in the United States. It is listed on Nasdaq (LIEN), is externally managed by Chicago Atlantic Credit Advisors, and earns interest income. Its customers are cannabis operators, and the financing is largely senior secured loans. It is a financial vehicle with no consumer profile and very low sponsorship potential.

Credo Semiconductor is a San Jose fabless chipmaker that designs high-speed connectivity products, including serializer/deserializer (SerDes) chips, active electrical cables and optical DSPs for data centres and AI clusters. Customers include hyperscale cloud operators and network equipment makers such as Microsoft and Amazon. Founded in 2008, it was listed on Nasdaq (CRDO) in 2022 and has grown rapidly on AI demand, with fiscal revenue of several hundred million dollars. It is a B2B component supplier with no consumer brand visibility.

Digital 9 Infrastructure (renamed Triple Point Digital Infrastructure) was a London Stock Exchange-listed investment company holding digital infrastructure assets, including subsea cables, data centres and fibre networks such as Elio, Aqua Comms, Verne and Emerald. It was managed by Triple Point and suffered a sharp share price fall, leading to a managed wind-down in 2024-25. It is an investment trust, not a consumer brand, and is of little use as a sponsorship prospect.

DNA X, formerly Sonim Technologies, is a Florida-based maker of rugged mobile phones and push-to-talk devices for first responders and industrial workers, sold through carriers like AT&T, Verizon and FirstNet. It was listed on Nasdaq (SONM) and has been renamed DNA X after a change of direction. Customers are enterprises, public safety agencies and utilities. It earns revenue from device sales and software. It is a niche B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Gurit is a Swiss composite materials company based in Zurich that develops and supplies structural core materials, kits, engineered composites and adhesives for wind turbine blades, marine, aerospace, automotive and industrial uses. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (GUR), it has annual sales in the hundreds of millions of Swiss francs and sites in Europe, Asia and North America. It has long worked in sailing and yacht racing, supplying composite materials to race boats. It is a B2B supplier with moderate visibility in marine and motorsport circles.

Hybe is a South Korean entertainment company based in Seoul, founded as Big Hit Entertainment and best known as the agency for BTS, with labels including Pledis (Seventeen), Source Music, Belift Lab and Ador (NewJeans), plus the Weverse fan platform and gaming and education businesses. It earns revenue from music, concerts, merchandise and fan membership. Listed on the Korea Exchange (352820) since 2020, it has a global fanbase and strong consumer brand visibility, especially among younger audiences.

JK Tyre and Industries is an Indian tyre manufacturer based in New Delhi, part of the JK Organisation. It makes truck, bus, passenger car, farm and two-wheeler tyres and sells them in India and export markets through a large dealer network. It operates plants in India and Mexico and other countries after acquiring Cavendish Industries and Cooper Tire's Indian assets. Listed on NSE and BSE, it is a recognised consumer-facing brand in India and has sponsored motorsport, including rallying and karting.

Navin Fluorine International is a Mumbai specialty chemicals company in the Mafatlal group that makes refrigerant gases, specialty fluorochemicals, pharmaceutical intermediates and offers contract development and manufacturing services. Customers include global pharma, agrochemical and refrigeration companies. It is listed on NSE and BSE, with annual revenue of several billion rupees and manufacturing in Gujarat. It is a B2B chemical supplier with no consumer profile and little sponsorship relevance.

Palfinger is an Austrian maker of hydraulic lifting, loading and handling equipment, including truck-mounted cranes, tail lifts, timber and recycling cranes, access platforms and marine cranes. Headquartered in Bergheim near Salzburg, it was founded in 1932 and is listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (PAL). It reports revenue of about 2 billion euros and sells globally through a dealer and service network. It is a B2B industrial brand with solid visibility among fleet operators and has some sports sponsorship history.

Pan Gulf Marketing is a Riyadh-based Saudi company categorised under manufacturing and office supplies, apparently marketing and distributing office and stationery-type products in the Kingdom. Its customers are likely retailers, schools and businesses, though the input does not confirm products in detail. The listing shows funding of SAR 440 million, dated December 2025, and a listed-company search status. It is a regional B2B supplier with moderate brand recognition in Saudi retail.

Perion Network is an Israeli-founded digital advertising technology company, now headquartered in New York, whose businesses include SORT (search), Content-based Display Advertising and an ad-tech platform serving brands, agencies and publishers. It is listed on Nasdaq (PERI) and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It earns revenue from advertising technology and a search partnership with Microsoft. It is a B2B company with modest brand awareness, mostly within the digital marketing industry.

Route Mobile is a Mumbai-based cloud communications platform provider offering A2P SMS, voice, email, OTT messaging, RCS and fraud-prevention services to enterprises and mobile operators worldwide. Founded in 2004 and listed on the NSE and BSE since 2020, it was acquired by Proximus Group (Belgium) in 2023-24 through its subsidiary BICS, which now holds a controlling stake. Customers include large banks, e-commerce and technology firms, and it is a B2B service with no consumer brand profile.

Sangoma Technologies is a Markham, Ontario provider of cloud communications, including unified communications, contact centre, VoIP phone systems, session border controllers and managed services under the Sangoma, Digium and Switchvox brands. It sells to small and mid-size businesses and service providers across North America and globally. It is dual-listed on Nasdaq (SANG) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (STC), with annual revenue of around US$250 million. It is a B2B technology brand with limited consumer awareness.

Sembcorp Industries is a Singapore-listed energy and urban solutions group (SGX: U96), providing power, renewable energy, integrated urban development and water services. Its businesses include thermal and renewable power in Singapore, India, China, the UK and the Middle East, plus industrial parks in Vietnam and Indonesia. Temasek Holdings, Singapore's state investment company, is a major shareholder. Revenue is in the billions of Singapore dollars. It is a B2B and utility brand, well known in Asian business but not a consumer product name.

Serge Ferrari is a French manufacturer of composite flexible materials, with a base in La Tour-du-Pin in the Isere, supplying coated technical textiles used in architectural membranes, awnings, sail and marine applications, sun protection and industrial uses. It is listed on Euronext Paris (SEFER) and sells to builders and manufacturers globally. It is a B2B materials brand, with moderate visibility in the architecture, yachting and sailmaking sectors but not with end consumers.

The Eastern Company is a Naugatuck, Connecticut manufacturer of industrial hardware, security products and metal castings, including locks, latches, rope, heavy-duty trucks hardware, and specialty vehicle closures. Founded in 1858 and listed on Nasdaq (EML), it serves industrial, transportation and security customers across North America and Asia. Annual revenue is several hundred million dollars. Its products are mostly B2B components, with low consumer brand recognition.

Tiandi (Jiangmen, Guangdong, China) is a food and beverage company, listed in the input as a listed-company result. The Crunchbase fields show about CN 862 million of funding, last dated February 2016, and nothing else about its products. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Torrance Precision is a Shanghai, China company categorised as industrial and industrial engineering, appearing in a listed-company search. The input shows about CN 852 million of funding, last dated May 2025. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Wealthnavi is a Tokyo-based robo-advisor offering automated investment management for retail customers in Japan, building diversified exchange-traded fund portfolios through its WealthNavi app. It was launched in 2016 and is one of Japan's largest robo-advisors by assets. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (WealthNavi, 2020), it earns a percentage advisory fee on assets, and also provides services to financial institution partners. It is a growing fintech with moderate consumer awareness in Japan.

WingArc1st is a Tokyo-based software company known for business intelligence and data tools, including Dr.Sum and MotionBoard, plus the SVF family for report output. It sells to large Japanese enterprises and public bodies. It listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4432) in 2019 and was taken private by Bain Capital in 2022. It is a B2B software vendor with strong brand recognition among Japanese corporate IT buyers but none among consumers.

ABEJA is a Tokyo AI company that develops deep learning and large language model platforms, including ABEJA Platform and Insight, mainly for retail, manufacturing and logistics customers in Japan. Founded in 2012 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Mothers market (5574) in 2020, it earns revenue from software subscriptions and AI development projects. It is a B2B technology brand with limited consumer awareness.

Agilysys is a software company that supplies hospitality management systems, including property management, point of sale, inventory and payment systems, to hotels, resorts, casinos, cruise lines, restaurants and stadiums. Founded in 1963 and headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia, it is listed on Nasdaq (AGYS) and sells subscriptions and services to operators worldwide. Revenue is around US$250 million. It is a B2B vendor with no consumer brand profile but strong standing among hospitality operators.

Australian Strategic Materials is a Perth-based company that is building a vertically integrated supply chain for critical metals, including rare earths, with a mine at Dubbo in New South Wales and a metal and alloys plant in Korea. It makes neodymium-based metals and alloys for magnets used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. Listed on the ASX (ASM), it sells to magnet makers. It is a B2B resource firm with little consumer awareness.

Boku is a San Francisco-based mobile payments company that lets consumers pay for digital goods and services using their phone bill or local wallets, serving merchants such as Spotify, Netflix, Google and Apple. It operates a network linking merchants to mobile operators and alternative payment methods across more than 90 countries. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (BOKU), with annual revenue near US$100 million. It is a B2B payments brand, known in the industry but not by consumers.

Calix is an Australian cleantech company based in Pymble, New South Wales, that develops a flash calcination technology for making reactive minerals, used in low-emission cement and lime, battery materials, water treatment and agriculture, and a carbon-capture process. It sells to industrial customers and research partners, and is listed on the ASX (CXL). It also has a US-focused battery materials program. It is a B2B science-led company with low consumer brand awareness.

Dekuple is a French digital marketing and data company based in Montreuil near Paris, operating in advertising, big data and direct marketing. It serves brands and advertisers in France with data-driven communication and customer acquisition services, and it appears in a listed-company search. It is a B2B agency-type brand with low consumer visibility and modest scale, so its sponsorship potential is limited.

Endurance Technologies is an Indian automotive component maker based in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra. It makes suspension systems, braking systems, transmission parts and aluminium die-cast components, mainly for two- and three-wheelers, with customers such as Bajaj Auto, Royal Enfield and Hero MotoCorp, plus European customers. Founded in 1985 and listed on NSE and BSE since 2016, it has annual revenue of more than 100 billion rupees. It is a B2B supplier with little consumer brand profile.

Frontier Digital Ventures is a Kuala Lumpur-based, ASX-listed (FDV) investor and operator of online classifieds and marketplaces in emerging markets, including Zameen in Pakistan, Fincaraiz in Colombia, Pointer in South Africa, Infocasas in Uruguay and Fazwaz in Thailand. It takes stakes in property and automotive portals. The portal brands are well known in their markets, but the holding company is mainly known to investors.

Goldmoney is a Toronto-based precious metals financial services company that allows customers to buy, hold and trade physical gold, silver and other metals in vaults, and to use them for payments and savings. It also runs a bullion wholesale business (Goldmoney Wholesale), and is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (XAU). Founded by James Turk in 2001, it holds billions of dollars of metal for customers worldwide. Consumer visibility is niche, mostly among precious metals investors.

Haidilao is a Chinese hot pot restaurant chain founded in Sichuan in 1994, known for table-side noodle-pulling, attentive service and free extras. Its holding company in Beijing is listed in Hong Kong (6862). It operates more than 1,300 restaurants in mainland China and abroad in Asia, North America, Europe and Australia, with annual revenue in the tens of billions of yuan. Haidilao is a very high-profile consumer brand in China and well known among Asian diaspora, and it has done sponsorship and partnerships.

Happy Forgings is a Ludhiana, Punjab-based Indian manufacturer of heavy forged and machined components for commercial vehicles, passenger cars, tractors, off-highway and industrial machinery, serving customers such as Tata, Ashok Leyland and other OEMs plus export clients. Listed on NSE and BSE in December 2023, it reports annual revenue of more than 12 billion rupees. It is a B2B supplier with low consumer brand awareness.

Hongjiu Fruit is a food and beverage company in Yubei, Chongqing, China, which the input categorises under fruit products. It appears in a listed-company search, with about CN 500 million of funding last dated November 2019. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ION Geophysical Corporation was a Houston company providing seismic data, software and equipment for oil and gas exploration, including marine seismic data libraries and software such as Gator and Orca, and its Concept Systems unit. Customers were oil and gas companies and seismic contractors. It was listed on the NYSE (IO) and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2022, after which its operations were sold. It was a B2B energy services brand with no consumer profile.

Luby's was a Houston-based cafeteria chain founded in San Antonio in 1947, operating Luby's Cafeterias, Fuddruckers burgers and Cheeseburger in Paradise restaurants, plus a culinary contract services business. It was listed on the NYSE (LUB), reached more than 100 restaurants, and in 2020 shareholders approved a plan to liquidate the company and sell its assets. Its restaurants had strong regional awareness in Texas, but it is now a wound-down company and not a sponsorship prospect.

Marsa Maroc is the main Moroccan port operator, based in Casablanca, handling container terminals, bulk, general cargo and passenger terminals at ports including Casablanca, Agadir, Jorf Lasfar and Tangier, and operating abroad as well. It is listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange (MSA), with a majority shareholder in the Moroccan state-linked group and investor group backing it. It is a B2B logistics operator with moderate national visibility but no consumer product.

Matinas BioPharma is a New Jersey clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing lipid nanocrystal (LNC) drug delivery technology and candidates such as MAT2203, an oral amphotericin B for fungal infections, and MAT2501. It is listed on the NYSE American (MTNB) and is funded by equity raises and partnerships. It is a small drug developer without commercial products, and consumers do not know the brand.

Namaste Technologies is a Toronto-based online retailer of vaporizers, smoking accessories and related products, which sold through websites in many countries and was listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (N) and the TSX Venture before restructuring. It changed its focus several times, including cannabis-related business. The input shows about $70 million of funding. Consumer awareness was modest and mostly online, and it ran into financial difficulties in the early 2020s.

Raksul is a Tokyo online platform for business printing and logistics, best known for its Raksul print ordering service for business cards, flyers and packaging, plus the Hacobu freight management and Novasell advertising businesses. It serves small businesses and enterprises across Japan. Founded in 2009 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4384) since 2018, it has revenue of over 50 billion yen. It is a B2B brand with moderate recognition among Japanese small businesses.

SEER Robotics is a Shanghai company that makes industrial automation products, including autonomous mobile robots (AMR), forklift automation, laser navigation and control systems for logistics, manufacturing and the new energy sector. It is a Chinese B2B robotics supplier that filed for a Hong Kong listing. The input shows funding of about CN 502 million in April 2025. It is not a consumer brand, and its customers are industrial firms.

Shakti Pumps is an Indian manufacturer of submersible pumps, motors and solar pumping systems based in Pithampur near Dhar, Madhya Pradesh. It sells to farmers, government programmes and infrastructure customers in India and exports to dozens of countries; solar pumps under agriculture subsidy schemes are a major part of its revenue. It is listed on NSE and BSE and has annual revenue of more than 10 billion rupees. It has regional brand awareness among Indian farmers.

Tesmec is an Italian company based in Milan that makes machinery and systems for building and maintaining power lines, fibre and gas pipelines, including trenchers, stringing equipment and railway-line monitoring and electrification systems. It operates in three segments, Energy, Trencher and Rail, and is listed on Euronext Milan STAR (TES). Customers are utilities, contractors and rail operators. It is a B2B industrial brand known in infrastructure circles, with little consumer visibility.

Three Squirrels (Sanzhi Songshu) is a Chinese snack food company founded in 2012 and based in Wuhu, Anhui, selling nuts, dried fruit, snacks and baked items mainly online through Tmall and other e-commerce platforms. It was among the first successful Chinese online-first food brands and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019 (300783). Revenue is in the billions of yuan. It is a high-visibility consumer brand in China with its cartoon squirrel mascots, though little known abroad.

Tongshifu is a Chinese company in Jiande, Zhejiang, categorised under e-commerce and handmade products. The input shows about CN 560 million of funding, last dated August 2018, and appears in a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

XA Investments is a Chicago-based firm categorised under accounting, advice and financial services. Its exact offering is not clear from the input, but it appears to be a financial advisory or investment management business serving United States clients. The input shows about $73 million of funding, last dated October 2025, and the row came from a search for listed companies, so a public listing is likely. It appears to be a low-profile financial brand with little consumer awareness, and its capacity for sponsorship spending is unknown. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

24SevenOffice is an Oslo-based cloud business software company offering an all-in-one platform for accounting, CRM, invoicing, project and time tracking, payroll and e-mail for small and mid-size businesses. Founded in 2000 and listed on Euronext Oslo Growth, it sells subscriptions through partners and accountants in Norway, Sweden, the UK and other European markets. It is a B2B brand with modest recognition among Nordic small business owners and no wider consumer profile.

Alexforbes is a South African financial services group headquartered in Sandown, Johannesburg, offering retirement fund administration, consulting, investment, insurance and financial advice to employers, pension funds and individuals. Formerly Alexander Forbes, it is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (AFH) and manages and administers hundreds of billions of rand for retirement funds. Its customers are mostly corporates and their employees. It is a recognised financial brand in South Africa, with moderate retail awareness.

American Lithium is a Vancouver-based exploration and development company advancing lithium projects, notably TLC in Nevada, Falchani in Peru and the Macusani plateau, which also holds uranium rights. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (LI) and Nasdaq (AMLI), and funds itself through equity raises. It has no revenue and no consumer products. It is a small resource developer with little public brand awareness and limited sponsorship capacity.

Arteris is a Campbell, California supplier of semiconductor interconnect intellectual property and system-on-chip design software, including FlexNoC network-on-chip IP used by chipmakers in automotive, consumer electronics and data centre chips. It licenses technology to customers such as Samsung, Qualcomm and automotive suppliers and earns royalties. Listed on Nasdaq (AIP) since 2021, with revenue of around US$60 million. It is a B2B technology firm with no consumer brand awareness.

BAIYU Holdings (formerly TD Holdings) is a Shenzhen-based company in commodity trading and supply chain services, especially non-ferrous metals, and precious metals-related financial services, listed on Nasdaq under the symbol BYU. It serves Chinese industrial and trading customers. The input shows about $45 million of funding, last dated November 2021. It is a B2B trading business with little public brand awareness.

Cipia is an Israeli computer-vision AI company, based in Herzliya, that provides in-cabin driver and occupant monitoring software and hardware, such as driver monitoring systems and fleet safety cameras, for automotive manufacturers and fleets. Formerly named Eyesight Technologies, it renamed itself Cipia and listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Its products help carmakers meet driver-safety regulation in Europe and elsewhere. It is a B2B automotive technology brand with no consumer awareness.

CY4GATE is a Rome-based Italian cyber intelligence and cybersecurity company, listed on Euronext Growth Milan (CY4), offering digital intelligence platforms for law enforcement and intelligence agencies, cyber defence products and training, plus the RTI business and the Cy4gate Group's subsidiaries. Customers are governments, defence bodies and large enterprises. It is a B2B brand known within the defence and security community, with no consumer profile.

Direct Digital Holdings is a Houston-based advertising technology company that provides programmatic advertising tools and services through its Colossus Media, Huddled Masses and Orange 142 businesses, connecting brands with multicultural and mid-market publishers. It is listed on Nasdaq (DRCT) and has had financial difficulties, with going-concern and delisting issues. It is a B2B ad tech firm with little consumer awareness and no public profile outside the digital advertising trade.

Dongpeng Teyin is a Chinese functional drink company based in Shenzhen, owner of the Eastroc Beverage brand and its Dongpeng Special Drink energy drink, sold in distinctive yellow bottles and popular with drivers, workers and young consumers in China. It also sells electrolyte water and other beverages. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (605499), it is one of China's leading energy drink makers by revenue. It is a major mainstream consumer brand in China with heavy marketing and sponsorship activity.

Ellos Group is a Swedish distance-selling and e-commerce group based in Boras, selling fashion, home furnishings and interior products through Ellos, Jotex and Homeroom brands, mainly in the Nordic countries. It serves consumers via online and catalogue sales and is a long-established retail name in Sweden, Norway and Finland. The input shows funding of SEK 400 million in December 2025. Ownership is private and should be checked. It has high household awareness in the Nordics.

Evercare is a Chinese company based in Beijing (Haidian) in the beauty, cosmetics and medical sectors, apparently offering aesthetic and healthcare services and products to Chinese consumers. The input shows about CN 350 million of funding, last dated April 2016, and the row came from a listed-company search. It is a domestic Chinese brand with little visibility abroad, and its current scale is not clear from the input.

Guestlogix was a Toronto-based travel commerce technology company that provided ancillary revenue software for airlines, cruise lines and travel brands, covering sales of insurance, hotels, ground transport and in-flight retail through airline websites and apps. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange before being acquired in 2018. Its ownership today should be checked. It was a B2B technology company with no consumer awareness, though airline passengers used its tools without knowing, and it has low sponsorship relevance.

Harte Hanks is a Chelmsford, Massachusetts-area marketing services company founded in 1923, offering customer experience, customer care, fulfilment and data-driven marketing services for large brands. Clients include retailers, financial and technology firms across the Americas, Europe and Asia. It is listed on Nasdaq (HHS), after earlier years as a newspaper and shopper publisher. It is a B2B agency with well-established industry recognition, but low consumer awareness.

ILOOKABOUT is a London, Ontario company working in analytics, databases and information services, known for online street-level imagery and geographic information tools for governments, utilities and commercial clients. The input shows funding of about CA$56 million, last dated March 2021, and the row came from a listed-company search. It is a B2B geospatial data business with low consumer brand awareness and a small scale compared with major mapping providers.

Jiumaojiu is a Chinese restaurant group based in Guangzhou, best known for its Tai Er sauerkraut fish chain, plus Jiu Mao Jiu, Song Hot Pot, Jiu Mao Jiu Cafe and other restaurant brands, operating hundreds of outlets in Chinese cities. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (9922) since 2020, it earns revenue from restaurant sales. Consumer awareness is high for Tai Er in China, but the group is little known abroad.

Koovs was an Indian online fashion retailer, based in Bengaluru, selling its own fashion label and third-party apparel and accessories to young women through its website and app. Listed on the London AIM market (KOOV) in 2016, it accumulated heavy losses and entered administration in 2020, after which its brand and assets were sold. It had moderate consumer awareness among young Indian shoppers, but is no longer a going concern.

Lakeland Industries is an Alabama-based maker of protective clothing for industrial workers, firefighters and first responders, including chemical suits, disposable coveralls and flame-resistant garments. Its customers are industrial companies, distributors and governments in the United States and abroad, with factories in Mexico, China, Vietnam and other countries. Founded in 1982 and listed on Nasdaq (LAKE), it has revenue around US$130 million. It is a B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Laox is a Japanese electronics and duty-free retailer, historically headquartered in Tokyo, that became a leading store for inbound Chinese tourists. It was majority-owned by China's Suning Group from 2009 and traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange before that group ran into difficulties and the retailer reduced its stores, later restructuring. It sold appliances, cosmetics and souvenirs. It was a recognised shopping name in Japan, especially among foreign tourists.

Mobiquity Technologies is a New York advertising technology company that offers programmatic advertising, location data and audience analytics services to brands and agencies, including through its Advangelists platform. It is listed on Nasdaq (MOBQ) and has recorded recurring losses. It is a small B2B ad tech firm that sells to marketers and has little consumer brand visibility and no public profile outside the digital advertising trade, so it is unlikely to be a sponsor.

MoneyOnMobile is a Mumbai-based mobile payments and financial services company that offered bill payments, recharges and cash services through retail agents and a mobile wallet in India. Previously Calpian, a Dallas company, it was listed in the United States and India. It targeted underbanked consumers and small retailers. Funding is shown at around $38 million. It operated as a niche fintech and had limited broader brand awareness.

Newtopia is a Toronto-based digital health company that offers personalised health coaching and genetic-informed lifestyle programmes to employers and insurers, targeting obesity, diabetes and chronic disease prevention. It is a B2B service whose customers are employers and benefit providers. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (NEWT), it raised about $46 million. It has low consumer brand awareness, since users come through employers.

NFON is a Munich-based provider of cloud telephony and unified communications for small and mid-size businesses, with the Cloudya and Nfon Business services sold in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and other European countries via partners. Founded in 2002 and listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (NFN) in 2018, it has revenue of around 90 million euros and an SME customer base. It is a B2B brand with modest awareness among European IT resellers.

PureCircle was a Chicago-based producer of stevia sweeteners, including high-purity Reb M and Reb D, sold to food and beverage manufacturers such as Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, and run by a global farming and processing operation. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange and Bursa Malaysia before being taken private by Ingredion in 2020. It is a B2B ingredient business, so consumers know the product category but not the PureCircle name.

Quhuo is a Beijing-based gig economy operator, listed on Nasdaq (QH), that manages fleets of delivery riders and drivers for food delivery, ride hailing and local life platforms in China. It provides operations management and staffing for platforms such as Meituan and Didi. It is a B2B labour services firm with low consumer visibility, although its riders are seen on Chinese city streets.

Raycloud is a Hangzhou-based Chinese e-commerce software and services company, offering cloud tools such as order and warehouse management for merchants on Taobao and Tmall, plus data and marketing services. It was listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and later became subject to Chinese regulatory and ownership attention. It is a B2B brand known among online merchants in China but with no international consumer awareness.

Remark Holdings is a Las Vegas company focused on AI and computer vision, with products such as KanKan facial recognition software, mostly sold in China, and had earlier digital media assets. It is listed on Nasdaq (MARK) and has had persistent losses, going-concern warnings and trading issues. It is a small B2B technology firm with low consumer brand awareness and limited sponsorship capacity.

Ruhnn Holding is a Hangzhou-based Chinese influencer marketing and e-commerce company that managed social media influencers and their fashion brands, selling apparel through Taobao stores. It was listed on Nasdaq (RUHN) in 2019. Revenue came mainly from product sales on e-commerce platforms, together with advertising and services. Its reach came through influencer fans, mostly young Chinese women, and it has little overseas awareness. It is a consumer fashion player with a B2B influencer management side.

Steel Exchange India is a Visakhapatnam-based steel manufacturer in Andhra Pradesh, producing TMT rebars, wire rods and structural steel from its integrated plant, and selling to construction and infrastructure customers. It is listed on the BSE and NSE and sells under the SEIL brand. Its customers are builders and distributors across southern India. It has regional brand recognition in Indian construction materials but is small by industry standards.

Stitch Fix is a San Francisco online personal styling service that sends curated clothing and accessories to customers based on style surveys and algorithms, with the option to keep or return items. It was founded in 2011 by Katrina Lake and is listed on Nasdaq (SFIX), with revenue of about US$1.2 billion and more than 2 million active clients in the United States and previously the UK. It is a consumer fashion technology brand with solid recognition in the United States.

Suja Life (Suja Juice) is a Californian maker of cold-pressed, high-pressure processed juices, smoothies and wellness shots, sold in grocery stores such as Whole Foods, Costco and Target across the United States. Founded in 2012 and based in Oceanside, it has been backed by large investors, with Coca-Cola reported to have taken a stake or ownership, so current ownership should be checked. Its customers are health-minded consumers. It is a well-known natural beverage brand in the US premium juice segment.

The Easou Technology is a Shenzhen-based Chinese internet company that built mobile search, reading and advertising platforms, including the Easou search engine and e-book content for feature phones and smartphones. It earned money from advertising and content. The input shows about $47 million of funding, with the latest round dated June 2025. It was once a notable Chinese mobile internet brand, but has little visibility today.

Tiny is a Victoria, British Columbia-based Canadian holding company, formerly Tiny Ltd, that acquires and operates internet and software businesses, including Dribbble, Flow, Hover, Pond, Giftlogic and Topline, and has operated as a long-term holder of small tech assets. Its funding is shown as CA$79 million. It is a B2B and creator-focused brand, with higher awareness for Dribbble among designers. It is not a mass consumer name.

Tracsis is a Leeds-based British technology company that provides software, data and consultancy for transport, particularly rail, and also traffic data, event traffic management and remote monitoring. Customers include train operators, Network Rail, councils and industrial clients. Listed on the AIM market (TRCS) and founded in 2004, it has revenue of around 80 million pounds. It is a B2B brand with limited consumer recognition.

Verimatrix is a French security company, based near Aix-en-Provence, that provides app protection, DRM and anti-piracy software for video, mobile and connected devices to pay-TV operators, streaming services and app developers. Formerly named Inside Secure, it was listed on Euronext Paris before a change of ownership. Its customers include large telecoms and media groups worldwide. It is a B2B security vendor with little consumer visibility, though its tools protect well-known platforms.

Vior is a Quebec-based Canadian mineral exploration company, in Brossard, listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, exploring gold and other properties, notably in the Belleterre area of Quebec. The input shows about $45 million of funding, last dated January 2025, and the Crunchbase category of business development. It is a small junior explorer with very low public brand awareness and no products sold to consumers.

Zahrat Al Waha for Trading and Contracting is a Riyadh-based Saudi manufacturer of plastics and building-related products, listed on the Saudi Exchange (Nomu). It produces plastic and plastic-related products for commercial and construction customers in the Kingdom. The input shows funding of SAR 150 million, last dated November 2025. It is a regional B2B company with little consumer brand awareness.

Acutaas Chemicals is an Indian specialty chemicals and pharmaceutical intermediates company based in Sachin, Gujarat, formerly Ami Organics, making advanced intermediates and active ingredients for pharma and electronic chemical customers worldwide. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2021, it supplies innovator and generic drug makers. Revenue is in the order of several billion rupees. It is a B2B manufacturer with no consumer visibility.

Axel Mark is a Tokyo-based Japanese company in advertising, gaming and telecom services, operating mobile game and digital content businesses such as app and advertising businesses, and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Mothers market. The input shows about $30 million of funding, last dated June 2018. It is a small Japanese digital media group with limited recognition outside its home market, and little information on its scale.

Crossject is a Dijon-based French specialty pharmaceutical company developing needle-free auto-injectors, notably Zeneo, with products such as Zeneo Midazolam for seizure emergencies and an adrenaline version, with US BARDA funding. It is listed on Euronext Paris (ALCJ). Customers are healthcare systems, military and emergency users. It is a small niche medical device firm with limited public awareness and revenue dependent on grants and early product sales.

Devsisters is a South Korean mobile game developer based in Seoul, creator of Cookie Run franchise games such as Cookie Run: Kingdom and Cookie Run: OvenBreak. It earns from in-app purchases from players worldwide, with Asian and Western markets, and licensing the characters. Founded in 2007 and listed on KOSDAQ (194480), it is a well-known mobile game brand with a strong fan base, especially among younger players.

Expert.ai is an Italian artificial intelligence company based in Modena, offering natural language processing and text analytics software, with a hybrid AI approach combining symbolic and machine learning methods, used by insurance, banking, publishing and intelligence customers. It was formerly Expert System and is listed on Euronext Growth Milan (EXAI). It is a B2B software company with limited consumer awareness.

Fanli (Fanli.com) is a Chinese cash-back and shopping rebate platform based in Shanghai, founded in 2006, that earns commissions from online merchants such as Taobao, JD.com and Amazon and returns part of the commission to users who shop through its site and app. It filed for a US IPO in 2018. Its customers are millions of Chinese online shoppers, and merchants pay for traffic. It is a recognised consumer deals brand in China, with little international awareness.

Future Supply Chain Solutions is a Mumbai-based Indian logistics company, part of the Future Group, that provided warehousing, transportation, e-commerce fulfilment and supply chain services for retailers and consumer goods firms. It was listed on NSE and BSE. After the Future Group's financial crisis and failed sale to Reliance Retail, its business suffered. It is a B2B logistics firm with low consumer awareness.

Gelion is a London-headquartered battery technology company, listed on the London AIM market (GELN), developing lithium-sulfur and zinc-bromide battery technology, with roots in the University of Sydney, and owning the Oxis Energy intellectual property bought in 2023. It targets aviation, defence and stationary storage customers. It is pre-commercial, with funding of about $35 million, and little consumer awareness, so it is not an obvious sponsor.

Hunan Haili Chemical Industry is a Changsha, Hunan, China company categorised under chemicals and industrial manufacturing. The input shows about CN 200 million of funding, last dated June 2025, and the row came from a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Kingswood is a London-based financial services firm, listed on the AIM market, that provided wealth management, investment advice and platform services in the United Kingdom, and was involved in the US market, formerly known as Kingswood Holdings. The input shows around 21.8 million of funding in March 2025. It is a small wealth manager serving individual and corporate clients, with little consumer brand awareness.

Locondo.jp is a Tokyo-based online fashion retailer, operated by Locondo Inc., that runs the Locondo fashion e-commerce site in Japan, selling apparel and accessories from several hundred brands to consumers, and was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Mothers market. Ownership should be checked. It is a consumer e-commerce brand with moderate awareness among Japanese fashion shoppers, and revenue comes from product sales and commissions.

Maase is a Chinese company shown in Guangdong and Jilin, categorised under advice, consulting and financial services. The input shows about $34 million of funding, last dated July 2025, and it came from a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Meliuz is a Brazilian cashback and loyalty company, based in Belo Horizonte, whose app and site return a share of purchases at partner retailers to members, and which also moved into digital banking and bitcoin treasury holdings. Listed on B3 (CASH3) since 2021, it serves tens of millions of registered users. It earns commissions from online merchants. It is a recognised consumer finance and shopping brand in Brazil and has marketing partnerships there.

Mopon is a Shenzhen, Guangdong, China company categorised under film, internet and travel. The input shows about CN 162 million of funding, last dated May 2015, and it appears in a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Myplas.com is a Shanghai-based Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for plastics raw materials, based in Hongkou, connecting plastic resin producers and traders with buyers and offering transaction and supply chain services. It earns commission and trading margin. The input shows funding of about CN 170 million, last dated July 2018. It is a B2B online marketplace with very low consumer awareness, known mainly in the Chinese plastics trade.

Network International is a Dubai-headquartered payments company that provides card issuing and merchant acquiring services, processing and digital payments across the Middle East and Africa, with customers including banks and retailers. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange (NETW) in 2019 and was taken private by Brookfield Asset Management in 2024. It is a B2B payments brand, known by banks and merchants but not by the wider public.

Pasofino Gold is a Toronto-based Canadian gold developer, listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, advancing the Dugbe gold project in Liberia. It has no production revenue and is funded by share issues and strategic partners. The input shows funding of about CA$47.7 million, last dated September 2025. It is a junior resource company without commercial output and minimal brand awareness.

PipGame is a Beijing-based Chinese online game and media company, categorised under gaming and entertainment, that developed and operated games and related media. The input shows funding of about $32 million, last dated December 2015, and the row came from a listed-company search. It is a niche domestic company with low visibility outside China, and the input gives no detail on its titles or user base.

Reliance Capital is an Indian financial services company, headquartered in Mumbai and part of Anil Ambani's Reliance Group, with businesses in insurance, asset management, broking and lending, such as Reliance General Insurance and Reliance Nippon Life. It was listed on NSE and BSE but went into insolvency in 2019-2021 and was acquired by IndusInd International Holdings (Hinduja group) through the insolvency resolution process. It was a high-profile consumer finance brand in India.

Sailvan Network is a Shenzhen-based Chinese cross-border e-commerce company that sells consumer electronics and other goods to overseas buyers through online marketplaces and trading platforms. It operates in B2B and B2C e-commerce. The input shows funding of about $37 million, last dated August 2017. It is an export-focused firm with low consumer brand awareness among overseas shoppers; sales growth depends on third-party marketplace policies.

SeaChange International is a Boston-area video software company, listed on Nasdaq (SEAC), that provides video streaming and delivery platforms for cable, telecom and media companies, including on-demand TV software. It was an early video-on-demand supplier and later restructured; Customers are service providers who license its software and services, and revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars. It is a B2B vendor with little consumer awareness and a small business by market-value standards.

Sensys Gatso Group is a Swedish-headquartered traffic safety and enforcement technology company, based in Jonkoping, formed in 2018 by the combination of Sweden's Sensys Traffic and the Dutch Gatso Group. It supplies speed cameras, red-light and tolling enforcement systems and services to governments, municipalities and police in Europe, the US and elsewhere. It is listed on Nasdaq First North Stockholm. It is a B2B brand known by public sector traffic buyers but not the general public.

Shequ e-fuwu is a Beijing (Haidian), China company categorised under consumer and food and beverage, and its name suggests a community e-commerce or services business. The input shows about CN 190 million of funding, last dated December 2018, and it appears in a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Solus Advanced Materials is a South Korean maker of electronic materials, based in Seoul, best known for copper foil for lithium-ion batteries and OLED materials, as the successor to Doosan Solus. Its customers are battery cell makers and electronics firms. It is listed on the Korea Exchange (336370). It is a B2B materials company with low consumer awareness, the successor to a Doosan group business.
